item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
Jill had a rectangular piece of paper.

[Image: A rectangle divided horizontally into two equal halves by a dotted line]

She cut her paper along the dotted line and made an L shape like this.

[Image: An L-shaped figure made of two rectangular strips]

Which of these statements is true?

options.label: A
options.text: The area of the L shape is greater than the area of the rectangle.

options.label: B
options.text: The area of the L shape is equal to the area of the rectangle.

options.label: C
options.text: The area of the L shape is less than the area of the rectangle.

options.label: D
options.text: You cannot work out which area is greater without measuring.

item.figure_description:
The first figure shows a horizontal rectangle with a dashed horizontal line dividing it into two equal top and bottom halves.

The second figure shows an L shape made from the two halves: one vertical rectangular strip on the left and one horizontal rectangular strip at the bottom right, joined along part of their edges at a right angle.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: Which rectangle is NOT divided into 4 equal parts?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: Rectangle divided into 4 equal smaller rectangles]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: Rectangle divided into 4 equal triangles]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: Rectangle divided into 4 equal horizontal strips]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Rectangle divided by three parallel diagonal lines]

reference_items.figure_description:
Four rectangular figures labeled A, B, C, and D, each partitioned into 4 regions:
- Option A: Divided into 4 equal quadrants by a vertical line and a horizontal line through the center.
- Option B: Divided into two squares by a central vertical line, with each square bisected by a diagonal from bottom-left to top-right, creating 4 identical right-angled triangles.
- Option C: Divided into 4 equal horizontal bands by three evenly spaced horizontal lines.
- Option D: Divided into 4 unequal regions by three parallel diagonal lines sloping up and to the right, creating two corner triangles and two trapezoids of unequal sizes.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Craig folded a piece of paper in half and cut out a shape.

[Image: Folded paper with cut-out shape]

Draw a picture to show what the cut-out shape will look like when it is opened up and flattened out.

descriptors: The drawing of the cut-out shape corresponds to figure A.
The drawing of the remaining piece of paper corresponds to figure B.
Drawings correspond to figures E or F or G.

reference_items.scoring_notes: Note: See the examples above. The accuracy in drawing is not important, nor is the size of the figure.
reference_items.figure_description: A vertical rectangular outline representing a piece of paper folded in half vertically. The vertical left edge is labeled with an arrow pointing to it and the word "fold". Along this folded edge, a cut-out profile is drawn: starting from a point on the left edge, a straight line segment angles up and right, turns back down and to the left to form a sharp inward notch, then curves outward to the right in a rounded semicircle, and finally curves back down and to the left to meet the folded edge at the bottom.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Three arrangements of 3 tiles labeled Rita, Ina, and Lana]

Rita, Ina, and Lana take turns arranging 3 tiles. Each arranges the tiles in a different shape as shown above. Which of the following is true about the area of the shapes?

options.label: A
options.text: Rita’s shape has a greater area than the others.

options.label: B
options.text: Ina’s shape has a greater area than the others.

options.label: C
options.text: Lana’s shape has a greater area than the others.

options.label: D
options.text: All of the shapes have the same area.

reference_items.figure_description:
Three arrangements of three tiles each, labeled "Rita", "Ina", and "Lana":
- Rita: Two squares are placed side by side horizontally, sharing a vertical edge. A triangle sits on top of the left square, with its base along the top edge of that square and its apex pointing upward.
- Ina: A square sits at the top with horizontal top and bottom edges. Attached below it is a triangle sharing the square's bottom horizontal edge and pointing downward. Attached to the lower-right edge of the triangle is a second square, tilted diagonally downward and to the right.
- Lana: Two squares are placed side by side horizontally, sharing a vertical edge. Attached to the right vertical edge of the right square is a triangle pointing to the right.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: six pieces of cardboard with length of the sides labeled in cm. Two of the pieces are square shaped with each side measured at 1 cm. Four of the pieces are rectangular shaped with two sides measured at 1 cm and two other sides measured at 2 cm.]

Susan has the 6 pieces of cardboard shown above. Which of the following shapes could Susan make using all 6 of these pieces without cutting them?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: Cube.]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: Triangular prism.]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: Truncated (or trapezoid) pyramid.]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Rectangular prism.]

reference_items.figure_description:
At the top of the item, six gray-shaded flat cardboard shapes are shown. Two are identical squares, each labeled '1 cm' on all four sides (top, bottom, left, and right). Four are identical horizontal rectangles, each labeled '2 cm' on the top and bottom sides and '1 cm' on the left and right sides.

The response options show line drawings of four 3D geometric solids with dashed lines representing hidden edges:
- Option A: A cube.
- Option B: A triangular prism resting on one of its rectangular faces.
- Option C: A truncated pyramid with a square or rectangular base and top.
- Option D: A tall right rectangular prism standing on a square base.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.figure_description:
Four shapes composed of identical square units are shown:
- Option A: A rectangle consisting of a grid with 2 rows and 3 columns (6 square units in total).
- Option B: A horizontal bar consisting of a single row of 6 square units (6 square units in total).
- Option C: A rectangle consisting of a grid with 2 rows and 4 columns (8 square units in total).
- Option D: A figure consisting of 6 square units arranged in two rows of 3 squares: a top row of 3 adjacent squares, and a bottom row of 3 adjacent squares shifted to the right so that its leftmost square is directly beneath the rightmost square of the top row (6 square units in total).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: Which shows 2/3 of the square shaded?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: Square divided horizontally into 5 strips]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: Square divided into three triangles]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: Square divided vertically into 3 unequal strips]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Square with an unshaded triangle]

options.label: E
options.text: [Image: Square divided vertically into 3 equal strips]

reference_items.figure_description:
Five identical squares, labeled A through E, each partitioned and shaded differently:
- Option A: The square is divided horizontally into 5 equal strips. The top 2 strips are shaded grey and the bottom 3 strips are unshaded (white).
- Option B: The square is divided by a diagonal from the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner, and a line segment from the center to the bottom-right corner. The entire upper-left triangular half is shaded grey, the right triangular section is shaded grey, and the bottom triangular section is unshaded.
- Option C: The square is divided by two vertical lines into three strips: a narrow shaded strip on the left, a wide unshaded strip in the middle, and a narrow shaded strip on the right.
- Option D: An unshaded triangle has its base along the entire bottom edge of the square and its apex at the midpoint of the top edge. The two right triangles flanking it on the left and right are shaded grey.
- Option E: The square is divided by two vertical lines into 3 equal-width vertical strips. The left strip and the right strip are shaded grey, and the middle strip is unshaded.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: In which of the following figures is the dotted line a line of symmetry?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: a dotted line dividing a square into two opposite trapezoids.]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: a dotted line dividing a rectangle into two opposite right angle triangles.]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: a dotted line dividing a pentagon into a trapezoid and an irregular pentagon.]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: a dotted line dividing a hexagon in the middle.]

reference_items.figure_description:
Four geometric shapes, each intersected by a dotted line:
- Option A shows a square with a tilted dotted line that enters through the top side near the top-left corner and exits through the bottom side near the bottom-right corner, dividing the square into two non-congruent trapezoids.
- Option B shows a horizontal rectangle with a dotted line running along the diagonal from the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner.
- Option C shows a regular pentagon with one vertex at the top and a horizontal base at the bottom. A slightly slanted, nearly horizontal dotted line cuts through the left and right sides below the center, dividing it into an upper portion and a lower trapezoid.
- Option D shows a regular hexagon with horizontal top and bottom edges. A vertical dotted line passes through the exact center, bisecting the top and bottom edges into two identical mirror-image halves.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

Chris has lots of tiles like this: [Image: Chris's tile]

Julio has lots of tiles like this: [Image: Julio's tile]

Pierre has lots of tiles like this: [Image: Pierre's tile]

Ben has lots of tiles like this: [Image: Ben's tile]

Who would need the least number of tiles to cover a classroom floor with his tiles?

options.label: A
options.text: Chris

options.label: B
options.text: Julio

options.label: C
options.text: Pierre

options.label: D

reference_items.figure_description:
Four rectangular/square outlines representing tiles, each shown to the right of a person's name:
- Chris's tile: a medium-small square.
- Julio's tile: a large horizontal rectangle, with both width and area visibly greater than all the other tiles.
- Pierre's tile: a small square, noticeably smaller than Chris's.
- Ben's tile: a medium-large square, larger than Chris's and Pierre's, but smaller in area than Julio's rectangle.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
